cards.title: Compartmental Model Parameters: Central Volume (Vc) and Flows
cards.claim: In compartmental modeling (e.g., Phoenix NLME), the central compartment is defined by a volume parameter (V) and concentration (C). The default elimination flow from the central compartment is parameterized as Clearance (CL). Inter-compartmental flows between central and peripheral compartments are parameterized as inter-compartmental clearance (Q). Vc is the volume of the central compartment and is distinct from NCA Vz or Vss. In 'Macro' models, concentration is modeled directly using a 'stripping dose' to derive volume, whereas 'Clearance' models use differential equations with explicit CL and Q parameters.
conditions: Vc is a structural parameter in compartmental models, not an NCA output.
In Clearance models, CL is a primary parameter; in Macro models, CL is derived.
Only one central compartment is allowed if microconstants are used.
Concentration parameters (C) are derived from Amount (A) and Volume (V) in amount-based models.
limitations: Vc is model-dependent and not directly comparable to NCA Vz or Vss without conversion.
Software-specific conventions (e.g., Phoenix NLME) dictate parameter names (CL, Q, V) and default flows.
Identifiability of Vc depends on the richness of the data and model structure.
cards.downstream_use: Use Vc and CL/Q parameters for mechanistic PK modeling, simulation of concentration-time profiles, and covariate analysis. Do not use Vc as a substitute for Vss in steady-state interpretation without model validation.
cards.retrieval_keywords: CL, CL/F, Vss, Vz and Vc definitions and conditions
